'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***The [[United States]] formally begins [[2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan|withdrawing]] its [[United States Armed Forces|troops]] from [[Afghanistan]] to mark the final phase of the end to its longest war. Additionally, [[NATO]] also starts withdrawing their [[troop]]s. [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-kabul-afghanistan-b06334b7f884e5392a92136ee03f610a (AP)]
**[[Taliban]] insurgents overrun an [[Afghan National Army]] base in [[Ghazni Province]], capturing dozens of troops and killing a "number of others". Acting Defense Minister General [[Yasin Zia]] confirms the fall of the security installation to the Taliban. [https://www.voanews.com/south-central-asia/taliban-overrun-afghan-base-capture-troops-us-nato-forces-exit (VOA)]
*[[2021 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan clashes|2021 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan conflict]]
**[[President of Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyz President]] [[Sadyr Japarov]] signs a decree that declares a two-day nationwide mourning effort for those who have died during [[Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border|border]] clashes with [[Tajikistan]]. [https://tass.com/world/1285731 (TASS)]
**[[Kyrgyzstan]] accuses Tajikistan of building up troops and [[military equipment]] on the border. The Kyrgyz side also accuses Tajik forces of opening fire on Kyrgyz vehicles in the area. A Tajik spokesman speaking from [[Dushanbe]] says the country was sticking to the [[ceasefire]] and withdrawal of troops. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/kyrgyzstan-accuses-tajikistan-amassing-troops-near-border-2021-05-01/ (Reuters)]
**Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan agree to a new ceasefire following border clashes, which includes withdrawing troops from the border. [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Minister]] [[Sergei Lavrov]] urges both countries to honor the agreement. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/1/kyrgyzstan-accuses-tajikistan-of-amassing-troops-near-border (Al Jazeera)] [https://en.trend.az/casia/kyrgyzstan/3417947.html (Trend News Agency)]
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**Seven members of the [[Kurdistan Region|Kurdistan]] military force [[Peshmerga]] are killed in an [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] attack in the [[Kirkuk]] [[Kirkuk Governorate|Governorate]]. [https://www.macaubusiness.com/7-kurdish-security-members-killed-in-is-attack-in-iraq/ (Macau Business)] [https://www.rudaw.net/english/kurdistan/010520213 (Rudaw)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]]
***Italian [[cruise line]] [[Costa Cruises]] returns to service for the first time in nearly five months following a ban of cruises by the [[Government of Italy|Italian government]] due to the pandemic. Several Costa ships had reported cases on board in the previous year. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1426208/costa-cruises-sets-sail-again-after-four-month-covid-19-break (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Bharuch hospital fire]]
**A hospital fire in [[Bharuch]], [[Gujarat]], [[India]], kills at least 16 [[COVID-19]] patients and two nurses. [https://www.thescottishsun.co.uk/news/7046284/india-covid-hospital-fire-latest-disaster/ (''The Scottish Sun'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****India reports a new global record of 401,993 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby marking the first time a country reported more than 400,000 new cases in a single day. This subsequently brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 19 million. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Spotlight/Coronavirus/India-s-daily-COVID-19-cases-reach-record-401-993 (Nikkei Asia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Osaka Prefecture]] reports a record 1,262 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/osaka-confirms-daily-record-1262-new-coronavirus-cases-saturday-nhk-2021-05-01/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Jordan]] reports its first three cases of the Lineage B.1.617 variant, which originally discovered in [[India]]. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/covid-jordan-detects-three-cases-of-indian-variant (''Khaleej Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****The [[Singapore]]an [[Government of Singapore|government]] bans all long-term pass holders and short-term visitors who have been in [[Bangladesh]], [[Nepal]], [[Pakistan]], and [[Sri Lanka]] in the last two weeks from entering or transiting through the country. It also tightens its [[Social distancing measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic|social distancing]] rules in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-30/singapore-reinstates-some-distancing-measures-tightens-borders (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****[[Syria]]'s rebel-held [[Idlib Governorate]] begins its [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccination]] campaign, with a 45-year-old nurse receiving the first dose. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1852196/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 21 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 224. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2108787/record-21-covid-deaths-1-891-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]]
****[[Kenya]]n [[President of Kenya|President]] [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] lifts the [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] imposed in [[Nairobi]] and surrounding counties, allowing bars, restaurants, schools, and religious services to reopen and revising the evening curfew to 10:00 p.m. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-05-01/kenyan-president-lifts-covid-19-lockdown-imposed-last-month (U.S. News & World Report)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Salvadoran political crisis]]
**The [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador]] votes to remove several judges from the [[Supreme Court of El Salvador|Supreme Court]] and remove Attorney General [[Raúl Melara]], both of which had been vocal opponents to the presidency of [[Nayib Bukele]]. The event is being referred to as a [[self-coup]] by the opposition and by news media outlets. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/constitutional-crisis-el-salvador-bukele-security-plan-200210183636678.html (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[International Space Station programme]]
**[[SpaceX Crew-1]]
***The four-[[astronaut]] crew of [[SpaceX]]'s [[SpaceX Dragon 2#Crew Dragon|Crew Dragon]] [[Crew Dragon Resilience|''Resilience'']] successfully [[Splashdown|splashes down]] in the [[Gulf of Mexico]] off the coast of [[Panama City, Florida]], arriving from a six-month mission aboard the [[International Space Station]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/spacex-capsule-with-4-astronauts-splashes-down-off-florida-nasa-2426329 (NDTV)]

'''Sports''' 
*[[2021 Kentucky Derby]]
**The 147th [[Kentucky Derby]] is held at [[Churchill Downs]] at a 50% capacity, with [[Medina Spirit]] winning the race. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kentucky-derby-2021-winner-medina-spirit/ (CBS News)]
